note: Discovery leads for nutrition topic workers (phase 4). LITERACY level: teach what each concept IS and WHY it matters, with original examples. Health-science content — accuracy is paramount: use Tier A government/authoritative sources for every claim. Biology/chemistry depth belongs to other subjects (reference only).

tierA.provider: USDA Food and Nutrition Information Center / MyPlate
tierA.useFor: dietary guidance, portion sizes, food groups (canonical U.S. guidance)
Nutrition Facts label rules, Daily Values, supplement labeling
digestion, metabolism, hydration, food safety consumer facts

THE backbone — ch. 1 (science of nutrition), 3 (digestion/absorption), 4 (carbohydrates), 5 (lipids), 6 (protein), 8 (energy balance), 9 (vitamins), 10 (minerals), 11 (water/electrolytes), 14 (lifespan). openstax.org blocks curl — read sections via Wayback captures of canonical URLs. REFERENCE_ONLY (no LLM ingestion)

tierB.provider: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health Nutrition Source

tierB.useFor: global nutrition facts (sodium, sugar, food safety)

cautions: ACCURACY: every numeric claim (calories per gram: 4/4/9, DRIs, DV percentages, fiber targets) must come from a cited source — never from memory. Dated figures carry their vintage.

NO MEDICAL ADVICE: no diagnosis, no treatment, no supplementation recommendations for the reader. Supplements lesson: what supplements are, how FDA regulates them (DSHEA, U.S. context), why labels differ from drugs — factual only.
NO DEMONIZING: no food shaming, no 'bad foods' framing; moderation language; sugars/fats taught factually.
FOOD SAFETY: CDC facts (temperatures, cross-contamination, at-risk groups) — factual, no scare content.
CONTROVERSIAL CLAIMS (fad diets, detox, superfoods): evaluated critically with evidence; evaluating-nutrition-claims owns the critical-thinking frame.
Biology (digestion, metabolism, absorption) is mechanistic at literacy level; cell biology depth belongs to other subjects (reference only).

Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D (≥1 C, ≥1 D per topic; max 3 of 5 per slot). Verify keys from the file yourself. BANNED: 'Which statement best defines X used in this lesson?' stems — write scenario questions.
